title: Choose the default Workers AI model for cloud runs: inventory, price, benchmarks
description:
The factory currently routes [orchestrator].model at workers-ai/@cf/openai/gpt-oss-120b — a placeholder picked because it was visible in the model list, not because it was chosen. Decide the default deliberately.

Three things to establish, in this order:
1. INVENTORY. Enumerate what Workers AI actually serves today on this account (GET /accounts/<id>/ai/models/search — the operator token already has ai read access). Record model id, context window, and whether it speaks the OpenAI-compatible shape the pi/omp kinds need. Do not work from memory or blog posts: the list moves, and this repo has been burned twice this epic by assuming platform behaviour.
2. PRICE. Workers AI bills per neuron/token; capture the actual unit price per model and convert to a comparable per-million-token figure. The point of the Workers AI rung is that inference bills to the same prepaid Cloudflare pool as compute and storage, so the comparison that matters is cost-per-completed-tick, not headline rate.
3. CAPABILITY. Compare against coding-agent benchmarks — DeepSWE and SWE-bench-family scores are the relevant ones for a harness that edits code and runs tests, far more than chat leaderboards. An orchestrator model that cannot reliably drive tool calls is worthless here regardless of price.

Operator-suggested candidates to evaluate (verify availability rather than assuming): the Qwen 3.x family, the DeepSeek families, and Kimi K3 if and when Workers AI serves it. gpt-oss-120b is the incumbent and must be in the comparison as the baseline it is.

Deliverable: a recommendation per ROLE/TIER rather than one global default — the orchestrator drives the skill loop and needs tool-use reliability, while economy implementers can trade capability for price. Say plainly where a Workers AI model is NOT good enough and a BYOK frontier model should stay in the table; the design explicitly expects a mixed routing, and a recommendation that pretends otherwise would be worse than none.

Pairs with kuf: that tick measures container start cost, this one measures inference cost. Together they price a wave.
notes:
2026-08-20 17:08 - EVIDENCE FROM A LIVE RUN (2026-08-20), and it makes this tick decisive rather than exploratory. run_5c3d7e4f booted perfectly on workers-ai/@cf/openai/gpt-oss-120b — model probe green, harness probe green, omp answered READY — and was given the correct prompt: 'continue the ticks skill's orchestrator loop to the end of epic 72y: waves, spawn, wait, collect, merge, integrated gate, close, review, closeout'.

It produced 271 bytes. It stated the resolved substrate, quoted the tk note it would record, and stopped. One turn. It did not enter the wave loop. Cost /bin/zsh.22.

So gpt-oss-120b reasons correctly and CAN call tools (xrz proved that separately) but does not SUSTAIN a long tool-using orchestration loop. That is precisely the capability this tick exists to measure, and it is why the recommendation must be per role: an orchestrator that stops after one turn is useless regardless of price, while the same model may be fine for a well-specified economy implementer.

Add to this tick's method: benchmark scores are a proxy — the decisive test for the ORCHESTRATOR role is whether the model completes a multi-wave loop end to end. Include that as an acceptance check for whichever model is recommended for [orchestrator].model.

Operator judgement, recorded: the DeepSeek v4 family is expected to be substantially stronger than the gpt-oss incumbent. kimi-k2.7-code and qwen2.5-coder-32b-instruct are the other code-specialised entries and belong in the comparison for the IMPLEMENT roles even if not for the orchestrator.

Note the pro/flash split maps naturally onto the tier vocabulary this repo already uses — pro for orchestrator and strong, flash for economy — which is the shape the recommendation should probably take rather than one global default.
2026-08-20 17:39 - [human] CORRECTION (operator, 2026-08-20): my earlier note put kimi-k2.7-code and qwen2.5-coder-32b-instruct forward as the code-specialised candidates. Both are a generation behind — qwen2.5-coder predates qwen3.8, and the kimi entries predate the current families. The leading Cloudflare-hosted candidates are DEEPSEEK V4 (pro-0813 / flash-0731) and QWEN 3.8 (qwen3.8-27b). Compare those; treat the older coder-tagged models as baselines at most.

DEEPSWE RESEARCH (together.ai/blog/deepswe; agentica-org/DeepSWE-Preview), and what it implies for OUR choice — DeepSWE is a coding agent trained from Qwen3-32B with pure RL: 42.2% Pass@1 on SWE-Bench-Verified, 59% with K=16 test-time scaling, +20 points from 200 RL steps.
  1. REASONING MODE MATTERS. Non-thinking mode gave 'limited performance improvement'. deepseek-v4-pro emits reasoning_content — it is a thinking model, which the research says is the property that counts for this domain. Check whether qwen3.8-27b exposes the same.
  2. CONTEXT LENGTH IS NOT THE LEVER. 16K -> 128K bought <=2%. Directly relevant to our cost: the live run re-sends ~77-79k input tokens EVERY turn (900k input tokens across 16 calls, $1.17 in seven minutes). If context is not buying capability, that spend is mostly waste and the orchestrator prompt/context strategy is worth attacking before the model choice is.
  3. DELIBERATE SUBMISSION. DeepSWE masks trajectories that hit max context, max steps or timeout, rewarding only deliberate submission — 'ensuring reward is only assigned when an agent deliberately submits encourages rigorous testing'. That is exactly the principle behind tick ehy: a run whose harness stops without durable evidence is not complete. Convergent, and worth stating in the recommendation.
  4. RL POST-TRAINING BEATS SCALE OR DISTILLATION. Pure RL from Qwen3-32B beat distilling from stronger proprietary models. So the selection question is which candidate has AGENTIC post-training, not which is largest.
  5. TRAJECTORY MULTIPLICITY over token scaling; most gains by K=8. Not applicable to a single orchestrator, but relevant if implementers are ever run as competing attempts.

LIVE EVIDENCE, which outranks any benchmark for the orchestrator role: gpt-oss-120b made ONE call and stopped. deepseek-v4-pro has sustained 16+ calls with real bash tool_calls and coherent reasoning about base branch, detached HEAD and the repo's PR+CI rule. Same prompt, same substrate, same probes — only the model changed.
2026-08-20 17:40 - [human] SUPERSEDES the DeepSWE-Preview figures in my earlier note — the operator was right that those pages are stale (Qwen3-32B base, 42.2% Pass@1, a generation old). CURRENT benchmarks as of August 2026:

  DeepSeek V4 Pro 0813 — 96.40% SWE-bench Verified, #2 overall behind only Claude Opus 5 (within 0.60 points), at roughly 1/36th the cost per test. GA 2026-08-13.
  Qwen 3.8-27B — 61.7 on SWE-bench PRO (a different and harder benchmark than Verified, so NOT directly comparable to the figure above). Released 2026-08-14. The Qwen 3.8-Max flagship has published no SWE-bench Verified result.

CRITICAL: the checkpoint Cloudflare serves as @cf/deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4-pro-0813 IS the 0813 GA checkpoint that scores 96.40%. The factory is already routed at it, so the orchestrator model question is close to answered — a near-frontier coding agent at open-weight cost, billing to the same Cloudflare pool as compute and storage.

CAVEAT for whoever completes this tick: do not put 96.40 (Verified) and 61.7 (Pro) in the same column. Either find both models on the same benchmark or state plainly that the comparison is not like-for-like. A recommendation built on mismatched benchmarks would be worse than none.

What survives from the DeepSWE reading is the DESIGN lessons rather than its scores, and they still hold: reasoning mode matters for agentic coding; context length is not the lever (16K->128K bought <=2%), which is pointed given our run re-sends ~78k tokens per turn; and reward only on DELIBERATE SUBMISSION, which is exactly tick ehy's principle.

Sources: codersera.com/blog/deepseek-v4-pro-0813-guide-2026, aimadetools.com/blog/deepseek-v4-pro-complete-guide, yottalabs.ai/post/qwen-3-8-benchmarks-what-is-verified-2026, vals.ai/benchmarks/swebench

I WAS WRONG TWICE and both corrections matter:
1. The '96.40% SWE-bench Verified, #2 behind Opus 5' figure I quoted is not a useful signal — DeepSWE puts deepseek-v4-pro at 63% against opus-5's 74%. Verified is saturated; this benchmark is not. Do not use Verified numbers in this tick.
2. gpt-oss does not appear on this leaderboard at all — consistent with it failing to sustain a single loop in our live run.

WHAT THE DATA SETTLES:
- deepseek-v4-pro at $0.24/task is ~49x cheaper than claude-opus-5 for 63% vs 74%. For a factory paying its own inference that is the value outlier of the table, and the operator's instinct was right.
- Among the operator's candidates: deepseek-v4-pro 63% > qwen3.8-max 57%. kimi-k3 scores 69%, ABOVE deepseek — but the account's Workers AI inventory has only kimi-k2.6/k2.7-code, not k3, so it is not available to this factory today. Worth re-checking when it appears.
- deepseek-v4-pro takes 155 STEPS, the highest of any model here, at 106k peak context. That is the profile of a model that grinds — which fits our live observation (16+ calls, ~78k input tokens re-sent per turn, $1.17 in seven minutes) and means the step count, not the per-task price, is what drives our real cost. Attack context strategy before model price.
- gpt-5.6-luna is remarkable at 67% for $0.61 — and it is what this repo already routes its balanced tier to locally. If a BYOK rung is ever wanted alongside Workers AI, that is the entry to beat.

METHOD NOTE for whoever finishes this tick: use this leaderboard, not SWE-bench Verified, and render it with agent-browser — WebFetch and curl return only the app shell.
acceptance_criteria: A committed comparison table of the Workers AI models actually available, with id, context window, OpenAI-compatibility, unit price and a per-million-token figure, alongside DeepSWE/SWE-bench-family scores where published; an explicit recommended model per role and tier with the reasoning; and a stated position on which roles should stay on a BYOK frontier model. Availability and prices are dated and sourced from the live API, not from memory.
